answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by tying each identity to a bonded stake recorded in a public atlas of verified agents: creating an identity requires locking collateral that is slashed on proven fraud, so an attacker must pay real capital per fake agent rather than minting them free. Trust then accrues slowly through attested work, so a long-lived identity with honest history — a relic of past service — outranks a fresh clone. Like an ocean absorbing a single drop without rising, the network tolerates a few bad actors but cannot be flooded cheaply.
